title: Right Triangle Trigonometry
presenterNotes: Emphasize that the six trigonometric functions are just ratios; students often memorize SOH‑CAH‑TOA but forget the reciprocals.
For special angles, draw the triangles on the board. The 30°-60°-90° and 45°-45°-90° triangles are worth memorizing.
When using calculators, walk around to ensure students are in degree mode. A quick check: sin 90° should equal 1.
Real‑life problems often involve adding eye level. Point out that the triangle only gives the height from the observer's eye, not from the ground.
The Blueprint block ties everything together. Use it to model a complete problem, then have students work in pairs on a similar problem.

teacherCues: Draw a right triangle and label the sides relative to an acute angle $\theta$. Ask: Which side is opposite? Adjacent? Hypotenuse?
Write the ratios for sine, cosine, and tangent. Ask: How are cosecant, secant, and cotangent related to these?
blocks.title: The Six Trigonometric Functions

explanation: Given a right triangle with acute angle $\theta$, the six [[kw:trigonometric functions]] are defined as ratios of side lengths.

The three primary functions: $\sin \theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$, $\cos \theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$, $\tan \theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$.
The three [[kw:reciprocal functions]]: $\csc \theta = \frac{1}{\sin \theta}$, $\sec \theta = \frac{1}{\cos \theta}$, $\cot \theta = \frac{1}{\tan \theta}$.
These ratios depend only on the angle $\theta$, not on the size of the triangle.
To evaluate, first use the Pythagorean Theorem to find any missing side, then compute the ratios.

visuals.title: Exact Trigonometric Values for Special Angles

explanation: The angles 30°, 45°, and 60° appear in [[kw:special right triangles]]: the 45°-45°-90° triangle and the 30°-60°-90° triangle.
For 45°-45°-90°: legs are equal; hypotenuse = leg $\times \sqrt{2}$. $\sin 45° = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, $\cos 45° = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, $\tan 45° = 1$.
These exact values can be used to find unknown sides in right triangles with these angles.
Write an equation using the appropriate trigonometric function, substitute the known exact value, and solve for the unknown.

confusionCorner.title: Degrees, Not Radians!
confusionCorner.body: These values are for angles measured in degrees. When using a calculator, make sure it is in [[imp:degree mode]]. If it's in radian mode, the results will be completely different.

explanation: [[kw:Solving a right triangle]] means finding the measures of all three angles and the lengths of all three sides.
Given one acute angle and one side, you can find the rest: the other acute angle is complementary (sum to 90°); use sine, cosine, or tangent with a calculator to find other sides.
For non‑special angles, set the calculator to [[imp:degree mode]] and use the SIN, COS, TAN keys.
If you need a reciprocal function (csc, sec, cot), use the reciprocal of the primary function: $\csc \theta = \frac{1}{\sin \theta}$, etc.
Always round answers to a reasonable number of decimal places based on the given data.

explanation: In many real‑life situations, you can form a right triangle and use trigonometry to find an inaccessible distance or height.
The [[kw:angle of elevation]] is the angle above the horizontal when looking up at an object. The [[kw:angle of depression]] is the angle below the horizontal when looking down.
Angle of elevation and angle of depression between two points are equal (alternate interior angles).
Identify the known side and the unknown side relative to the given angle. Choose sine, cosine, or tangent based on the sides involved.
Set up an equation, solve for the unknown, and interpret the result with appropriate units.

questions.prompt: The angle formed by a horizontal line and the line of sight to an object above is the angle of ___.
A 100-foot tall lighthouse casts a beam at a 12° angle of depression. How far from the base does the beam hit the water? (Round to nearest foot, enter a number)
If the angle of elevation to the top of a tree is 45° from a point 50 feet away, how tall is the tree? (Enter a number)

confusionCorner.body: When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate interior angles are equal. The horizontal lines from the observer and the object are parallel, so the angle of elevation and angle of depression are [[imp:equal]]. Use this to set up the correct triangle.

explanation: [[imp:Understand]]: Read the problem carefully. Draw and label a right triangle. Identify the given angle and side, and determine which side is unknown. Determine the correct trig function (sin, cos, tan) that connects them.
[[imp:Solve]]: Write the trigonometric equation. Substitute known values. Solve for the unknown. Use a calculator set to degree mode for non‑special angles.

blocks.title: Blueprint Aid — Solving Right Triangle Trigonometry Problems

discoveryHook.scenario: Whether you're finding the height of a skyscraper or the width of a river, the Blueprint for right triangle trigonometry keeps you on track: understand the situation, set up the right trig equation, solve, and interpret the result.

examples.title: Example A — Jin Mao Building Height (Blueprint)
steps: Understand: Draw a right triangle. Adjacent side = 75 m, angle = 80°. Opposite side = height above eye level ($h$). Use tangent.
Conclude: Building height = $h + 1.5 \approx 426.8$ m. (The actual height is about 421 m, so close!)
examples.prompt: Your eye level is 1.5 m above ground. From 75 m away, the angle of elevation to the top of the Jin Mao Building is 80°. Find the building's height.
